concepts.def: Pollution from a single identifiable location (factory pipe, oil spill).
Diffuse pollution from many sources (urban run-off, agricultural fertiliser).
Released directly into the environment, e.g., SO2 from coal combustion.
Formed by reaction of primary pollutants, e.g., tropospheric ozone, sulfuric acid.
Toxic compounds resistant to degradation, e.g., DDT, PCBs; covered by Stockholm Convention (2001).
PM10 and PM2.5: airborne particles linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pollution — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Pollution brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Pollution.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Run-off from many farms is which kind of source?
options: Point
Non-point
Stack
Effluent
CFCs
POPs
GHGs
NOx

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Bacteria produce them.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Bacteria produce them.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Secondary pollutant”?
options: Released directly into the environment, e.g., SO2 from coal combustion.
Toxic compounds resistant to degradation, e.g., DDT, PCBs; covered by Stockholm Convention (2001).
Diffuse pollution from many sources (urban run-off, agricultural fertiliser).
Formed by reaction of primary pollutants, e.g., tropospheric ozone, sulfuric acid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Point source”?
options: Diffuse pollution from many sources (urban run-off, agricultural fertiliser).
Toxic compounds resistant to degradation, e.g., DDT, PCBs; covered by Stockholm Convention (2001).
PM10 and PM2.5: airborne particles linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease.
Pollution from a single identifiable location (factory pipe, oil spill).
